_comments: TogetherLedger engine settings. Edit values, never keys.
Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation only.
timezone .......................... IANA zone. All dates evaluated here.
forecast_days ..................... How far the forecast engine projects.
minimum_safe_balance .............. The cash floor. A projected day below this is a
risk even when it stays positive. Also the buffer
held back from safe discretionary.
large_payment_threshold ........... A bill at or above this gets its own risk check.
SPENDING, not aspiration: 19 statements show
change in spending.
discretionary_lookahead_days ...... Days past the week end whose bills are reserved
before declaring money safe to spend.
alert_reminder_days ............... An unchanged risk is re-sent after this many days.
balance_max_age_hours ............. A balance older than this is stale; the daily
email will not send on it.
parser_model ...................... Anthropic model that reads uploaded screenshots.
discretionary_exclude_keywords .... Descriptions never counted as discretionary.
paycheck_matching_keywords ........ Substrings that identify income deposits.
sms_enabled ....................... Legacy SMS path. Email is the primary channel;
this stays false unless deliberately re-enabled.
daily_discretionary_allowance ..... DERIVED, not chosen. Everyday spending that is not
already an explicit bill. Computed from the last 12
months of statements: total debits, minus everything
matching a modelled bill, minus obligations that have
since ended (Ally, Aetna, school tuition), over 364
days including the December peak. Came to $110.56/day.
It fell from $216.98 because groceries and fuel became
explicit bills rather than being buried in here.
Recompute when the bill list changes materially -
otherwise spending gets counted twice or not at all.
CALIBRATION, as of 11 Aug 2026. Modelled outflow is $18,677/month against $16,175
of actual average debits, and modelled income is $14,866 against $16,097 of actual
credits. The model is deliberately more pessimistic than history on both sides:
* variable bills forecast at their observed monthly maximum, not the average;
* the Loew & Patel braces placeholder is $400/month, a pure guess - the statements
show $1,000 once and small irregular amounts, so this is the single largest
unverified number in the ledger;
* income counts payroll only, while actual credits also include Venmo cash-outs,
Zelle received and refunds, which are real money but not dependable income.
Historical debits also still contain roughly $1,836/month of payments since
renegotiated away, so post-renegotiation reality should run below $16,175.
Recheck this against fresh statements before trusting the size of any shortfall.
